title: Integer extension by zero embeds in the constant integer sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be any topological space and $U\subseteq X$ any open subset. There exists a monomorphism $j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_U\to\underline{\mathbf Z}_X$, where the constant sheaf is [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and extension by zero is [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero]. Neither $X$ nor $U$ is required to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Lemma 02UX (lemma-vanishing-generated-one-section), third paragraph, kernel viewed as a subsheaf of the constant integer sheaf

proof.text: Identify the restriction of the constant integer sheaf C on X with the constant integer sheaf on U. In Lean this follows from overPullbackConstantSheafIso, the equivalence between the slice of opens over U and opens of U, and pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility for that equivalence. These identify sheafifications of the same constant presheaf. Extend this identification by zero and compose with the counit j_!j^*C to C.

For x in U the extension-by-zero stalk theorem identifies the composite of the interior stalk isomorphism and the stalk of the counit with the restriction-stalk isomorphism. The counit stalk map is therefore an isomorphism and is monic. Outside U the source stalk is zero, so the stalk map is monic there too.

By the stalkwise monomorphism criterion the counit is monic. Extension by zero carries the restriction identification to an isomorphism, so its composite with the counit is also monic. Empty U and U=X are included.
